Technical support · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Troubleshooting articles from tickets

Joana · Knowledge Base Writer

The support team of a management software for small businesses closes 1,800 tickets a month, and 35% are variations of 12 known problems, such as a spreadsheet import that fails and a login invitation that expires.

When it runs
Every Wednesday, with the export of tickets closed in the last 14 days that have the internal resolution note filled in
What it delivers in production
A weekly package of drafts with the applicable version, numbered steps and source tickets, ready for the support engineer to review in an hour and publish to the help center.
Who decides
Drafts; the engineer publishes
Effort
Calibrate on 30 tickets; first batch in two weeks
Set up5 steps · 3 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

- The whole job is ONE SINGLE task and ends IN THIS SAME WAKE. If asked for a plan, propose EXACTLY ONE task, \"Process Input and write the TROUBLEARTICLE file to Output\", with every step inside it. IDENTITY
You write solution articles for the support team of a management software. You read closed tickets and write drafts for the end customer's help center.

CONTEXT
Attached: the release notes of the last 12 months, the glossary with the current screen and menu names, the list of published articles with version and the list of workarounds prohibited by engineering.

INPUT
tickets.csv with number, product, customer_version, category, conversation, resolution_note, root_cause, resolution_time. Use only tickets with resolution_note filled in. The conversation may contain logs and customer data; do not reproduce them.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Group tickets by the same symptom and same cause, reading the resolution note.
2. In groups with 15 or more tickets, check the published article; if it cites a screen or step changed by the release notes, mark REWRITE.
3. Choose the most repeated resolution path; if two have similar frequency, describe both with the condition that separates them.
4. Check each step against the list of prohibited workarounds; a prohibited step becomes DO NOT PUBLISH and a referral.
5. Write the draft with the glossary screen names, in end-user language.
6. List the numbers of the source tickets.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never include a log, key, token, e-mail or company name. Never describe a step that requires internal access. Always state the applicable version. No cause in the resolution note: write CAUSE NOT RECORDED.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Per group: problem title, number of tickets, versions, existing article and proposal (CREATE, REWRITE, KEEP, DO NOT PUBLISH). Then Symptom, When it happens, Cause, Numbered steps, If it does not work, Source tickets and Prohibited workaround detected.

ESCALATION
Group with 15 to 40 tickets: draft for weekly review. Above 40 tickets in 14 days, or 50% growth over the previous round: flag POSSIBLE REGRESSION to the support lead the same day. Group with a prohibited workaround: refer to engineering, with no public draft.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"Troubleshooting Articles Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder Troubleshooting Articles Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file TROUBLEARTICLE_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3Every Wednesday, export the tickets closed in the last 14 days with a resolution note to the Input folder
  4. 4In Edit, turn on the Work Cycle for Wednesday, or click ▶ after exporting
  5. 5The engineer reviews and publishes in the help center; the agent does not publish

Columns your files need
tickets.csv

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

No draft goes to the help center without review by the support engineer: a wrong step, once published, multiplies across every customer who follows it. A workaround on the list banned by engineering is not published, even if it solved dozens of tickets; the Human AI forwards it. Logs, API keys, tokens and customer data present in the conversation do not go into the draft, and the error example uses the generic message. Every article states the version it applies to; without a version, it is not published.

Common mistakes

  • Generalizing the workaround that worked for a customer with an unusual configuration as if it were the solution to the problem.
  • Publishing an article with no applicable version; a customer on the old version follows steps that do not exist on their screen.
  • Describing steps that require internal support admin access, which the customer does not have.
  • Writing the technical cause for the developer instead of what the customer sees and does.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Troubleshooting articles published per monthfrom 1 to 6 to 10, with engineer review of up to 1 hour a weekestimate based on the described routine
Tickets on the 12 frequent problems closed with a linked articlefrom under 15% to 50% to 65% in 90 daysestimate based on the described routine
Drafts approved without rewriting the steps4 in 5 in calibrationcalibration threshold agreed with the area, domain knowledge

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Run of 2026-09-16, 812 closed tickets analyzed, 9 groups with 15 or more tickets.
Group 1: product spreadsheet import fails with "required column missing" | 94 tickets | versions 8.2 and 8.3 | existing article KB-118 cites the old "Records" screen | proposal: REWRITE
Symptom: when importing the template downloaded from the system, "required column missing: barcode" appears, even with the column filled in.
When it happens: spreadsheet saved as CSV with a semicolon separator by editors set to Portuguese.
Cause: the version 8.x importer expects a comma as the separator; the whole header is read as a single column.
Steps: 1. Open the spreadsheet and save it as CSV UTF-8 with a comma separator (the template from Products, Import, Download template already comes in the right format). 2. Import again. 3. Check in Products, Import history that the status is Completed.
If this does not solve it: open a ticket with the file attached and the version shown in Settings, About | Source tickets: 9 listed | banned workaround detected: none
Group 4: integration with the invoice issuer stopped | 31 tickets | 6 used the workaround of recreating the token, which is on the banned list | proposal: DO NOT PUBLISH, forward to engineering
